method: simulated LLM-ranker reliability sweep (real kimi run hung; see note)
real_kimi_note: The real-LLM frontier hung 1h22m on a network call (urllib timeout did not fire; server held the connection). kimi-for-coding measured ~30s/call and returned degenerate rankings on the abstract task -> operationally fragile + task-fit-poor. Switched to a controllable-reliability simulation: the architectural question is p (LLM reliability) x D, not one flaky model.
verdict: FRONTIER FOUND — fixed-half-budget HYBRID is fragile; its win is an easy-corner artifact
reading: The ADR-0046 HYBRID win (perfect + half cost) held only in the EASY corner (D=4, clean confound, lucky LLM). At realistic LLM reliability (p<1.0) or higher D, the fixed-half-budget 'trust the un-tested tail' MISSES true causes -- a CORRECTNESS failure, not just inefficiency. At p=0.9 (~ real kimi on an easy task) HYBRID already drops to ~1.8/2; at p~0.5 (abstract-hard) it loses ~half the causes. Min reliability for ~2/2 at half budget is essentially p=1.0 -- i.e. only a near-perfect LLM makes fixed-half-trust safe.
architecture_refinement: The frontier reveals that the fixed-half HYBRID VIOLATED the founder's own governance principle ('policy only acts on VERIFIED findings, never trusts the LLM directly'): trusting the un-tested tail IS acting on unverified LLM judgment, and that is exactly what fails. The corrected design: (1) the verification fraction must ADAPT to LLM-reliability x stakes (verify deeper when the LLM is less reliable or the cost of a missed cause is high); (2) for the un-verified tail you ESCALATE (human/disposer) or verify more -- you do NOT silently trust it. So the governance principle is MORE load-bearing than it first appeared; HYBRID's efficiency is real only in the high-reliability / low-stakes corner.
operational_finding: The LLM organ is also operationally fragile (slow ~30s/call, can hang past timeouts, task-fit-dependent) -> the system must never BLOCK on it: hard timeouts + graceful degradation to CWM-verify + escalation. This is a real cost of track A the architecture must budget for.
